newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RUTHERFORD FINED FOR BREACHING CODE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RUTHERFORD FINED FOR BREACHING CODE.

text.p: Transvaal captain Ken Rutherford has been fined 500 rand for breaching the United Cricket Board of South Africa's (UCBSA's) code of conduct, officials said on Wednesday.
Rutherford was also suspended for one match -- suspended to the end of the 1997-98 season, UCBSA managing director Ali Bacher said in a statement.
Rutherford was found guilty of contravening three sections of the code of conduct on the last day of Transvaal's recent Supersport Series cricket match against Eastern Province.
"He (Rutherford) showed his displeasure by throwing the ball to the ground and verbally challenging a decision by the umpire (Dave Orchard) to turn down an appeal for a catch," Bacher said.
"At the end of that over, he made remarks about the umpire's inability to make proper umpiring decisions. In doing so, he used abusive language."

Bacher said Rutherford, both with his international experience with New Zealand and his status as a provincial captain, had a duty to ensure that the code of conduct was respected and adhered to at all times.
